### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `652912eec4fa37a3e92d38ceb567bdb0bb3efe12` — the merge of head `b10abccd2b2f5123b414f10936b174cb49226bf5` into base `93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 652912eec4fa37a3e92d38ceb567bdb0bb3efe12 && git checkout 652912eec4fa37a3e92d38ceb567bdb0bb3efe12
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f b10abccd2b2f5123b414f10936b174cb49226bf5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f && git merge --no-ff b10abccd2b2f5123b414f10936b174cb49226bf5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b4ee77cd395e506b6aab3d1bb53415d3422f523b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + platform-tool-names.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.test.ts, 11 packs under ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/, .changeset/37190-get-record-context-platform-tool.md
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments
- `get_record_context` sits in the `service-ai` group, in sorted position, and stays in `MCP_DOOR_TOOL_NAMES`. The docblock matches ADR-0160 D4 (line 229: the group gains the name with cloud's registration).
- No rule code changes. The lint universe is seeded from `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES`, so the `mcpOnly` arm stops firing for this name on a `mcpPrompt: false` skill. The new lint test pins false, true and unset, with `get_record_contexts` as a control that is still reported.
- No gate in this repo compares a group with what cloud registers, and every check-run on the head is success or skipped.
- The exact-set gate is in cloud: `packages/service-ai/src/__tests__/platform-tool-names-conformance.test.ts` asserts `toEqual` against the pinned spec.
- **Locales.** All 11 packs carry the key once, directly after `get_record`, in each pack's quote style. The translations read sensibly: zh-Hans 读取记录资料, zh-Hant 讀取記錄資料.

### ② Semver level
- `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@object-ui/i18n` is right: a non-protocol change ships `patch` under AGENTS.md step 3.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: `SkillSchema.tools[]` accepts the same strings.
- `@objectstack/lint` needs no entry of its own, since only a test moves.
- **`Clause-②: no` is wrong.** The exported `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE` and `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` gain a member, and `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` stops reporting a name it reports today. Main has a precedent for exactly this: `.changeset/35036-mcp-door-tool-names.md` declares `Clause-②: yes (widening)` for "`ai-skill-tool-unresolved` stops warning on eight tool names", with spec `patch`.

### ③ Boundary flags
- **Landing order.** Merging this alone turns no objectstack gate red. But a cloud pin move past this merge that does not also register the tool fails cloud's service-ai conformance test. So the pin move must be the cloud#4978 PR itself, and an unrelated cloud pin bump past this merge is blocked until then. The card's rule covers this (hold until cloud#4978 is ready), and the PR is a draft.
- **Author-facing gap.** A spec release cut between this merge and cloud serving the tool would leave `os lint` silent on a `mcpPrompt: false` skill naming the tool. This is advisory only, and the card bounds it with "does not merge alone into a release".

### ④ Design judgment
The PR adds one constant entry plus the labels the registry's maintenance contract asks for, with no new mechanism. Pinning that the name is absent from `service-ai-studio` is reasonable.

### Findings
- **R1 (must-fix).** `Clause-②: no` → `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the PR body and the changeset. The level and `Metadata-protocol` stay as they are.
- **R2 (nit).** Add `Skills-docs: none` to the changeset, as sibling changesets do. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` points at the registry file and names no tool, so no skills edit is owed.
- **R3 (note).** Keep this PR in draft until cloud#4978's PR is ready, and have that PR's pin move name this merge sha.

- `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@object-ui/i18n` are correct (AGENTS.md step 3).
- `Skills-docs: none` is accurate.

- **Author-visible gap.** Unchanged and accepted. It is advisory only and bounded by the card's rule that this does not merge alone into a release.

### ④ Design judgment
Unchanged: one constant entry and the labels the registry contract asks for, with no new mechanism.

### Findings
- R1 (must-fix, `Clause-②`): resolved in the changeset and the PR body.
- R2 (`Skills-docs` line): resolved.
- R3 (hold in draft and name the cloud PR): resolved in the body; the PR is a draft and names cloud#4987.
- No new findings.
